content.title: Accounting workflow
content.body: Create a customer invoice, record a supplier bill, categorize a bank transaction and reconcile a payment. Include a refund, duplicate and correction. Check that each action is traceable and that reports agree with the underlying ledger.

content.title: Bank reconciliation and reporting
content.body: Test the actual bank feed and the exception workflow for unmatched transactions. Verify that the finance team can identify duplicates, fees and transfers without losing audit context. Run the reports needed for close and compare them with the existing system.

content.title: Tax and jurisdiction
content.body: Confirm the relevant regional edition, tax rates, filing needs, currency handling and supported business types with the vendor and accountant. Do not assume that a product available in one country supports the same functions or rules everywhere.

content.title: Migration and integrations
content.body: Export a sample of contacts, invoices, bills, accounts and transactions. Validate opening balances and reconcile the first period. Test integrations with payroll, payment, inventory or expense systems and document what happens when a sync fails.

content.title: Cost and governance
content.body: Request current pricing for the exact users, entities, currencies and required integrations. Include payment fees, migration, training, support and accountant access. Review permissions, audit history, backups, export and renewal terms before committing.

content.title: Pilot acceptance criteria
content.body: Process a sample invoice, bill, payment, bank reconciliation and month-end report. Reconcile the totals to an independently checked sample and record every manual adjustment. Ask the accountant to confirm that the reports and export formats support the business's actual close process.

content.title: Failure cases and migration
content.body: Test duplicate transactions, a refund, an unmatched bank item, a changed tax code and a failed integration. Validate opening balances and historical transaction mapping before a full migration. Keep the old records available until the finance owner signs off.

content.title: Decision record
content.body: Document local tax and reporting needs, entities, currencies, users, bank connections, integrations, accountant access, backup and export requirements. Request current written pricing for the exact setup. Include training, payment fees, migration and ongoing reconciliation in the total cost.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Xero?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Xero when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Test a representative task and verify current capabilities and limits directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: How should a team test Xero?
faqs.answer: Use the same real input, expected outcome and acceptance criteria each time. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown, including setup time, manual work and failure handling.

faqs.question: Which limitations should be checked in Xero?
faqs.answer: Check the exact plan, integrations, permissions, export, data retention, recovery and ongoing administration. Treat untested or undocumented capabilities as unknown until confirmed.

faqs.question: Are Xero prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, plan limits and independent ratings are not verified in this review. Check official documentation and obtain a dated quote before purchase.

faqs.question: What should be confirmed before adopting Xero?
faqs.answer: Confirm the core workflow, access controls, integrations, data export, account offboarding, support responsibilities and renewal terms. Assign an owner for the implementation and ongoing review.

author: Emily Nakamura
difficulty: Not independently assessed; validate with a pilot
learningCurve: Not independently assessed; validate during a pilot
whoShouldUse: Can be evaluated for a cloud-based bookkeeping and financial reporting workflow. A structured pilot can test invoicing, bank reconciliation, permissions, and reports with real sample data. Data export and integration checks can help reduce migration risk.
whoShouldNotUse: Plan limits and regional accounting features require direct confirmation. Bank feeds, add-ons, payroll, inventory, and other integrations may add cost or complexity. Migration needs careful reconciliation of opening balances and historical records.
